topic: Unitree Unveils 'Guardian' Robot That Lifts Cars and Disarms Attackers
angle: Breaking down the mechanical torque and AI vision behind Unitree's new guardian robot, explaining how electric actuators can deliver enough raw power to flip vehicles and disarm human threats in tactical scenarios.
why: Robot-focused Shorts are driving tens of millions of views across YouTube this week (with top clips reaching 7M to 11M+ views), showing massive global appetite for physical machines. With this news published on October 22, 2026 and major science explainer channels yet to cover the mechanics behind it, Tomorrowly can capture immediate search and browse traffic.
facts: Robotics company Unitree has officially unveiled a new heavy-duty security system designated as a 'guardian' robot (reported October 22, 2026).
The new platform is designed specifically for public safety, high-risk security, and tactical emergency interventions.
Unitree claims the robot possesses sufficient raw power to lift passenger cars during rescue or clearance operations (claimed).
The manufacturer claims the system can physically intercept and disarm hostile attackers in close-quarters scenarios (claimed).
To achieve car-lifting capability without traditional bulky hydraulics, the system uses ultra-high-torque electric joint actuators combined with reinforced high-stress alloys.
The platform utilizes multi-sensor spatial awareness, including LiDAR and depth cameras, to map environments in real time.
Integrated AI vision models are trained to track fast human movements and identify weapons or threatening gestures within milliseconds.
Traditional tactical robots were limited to slow bomb disposal tracks, whereas modern legged and hybrid platforms can traverse rubble, stairs, and uneven terrain.
Unitree has previously developed agile quadruped robots (such as the Go2 and industrial B2) and general-purpose humanoid robots (G1).
Deploying autonomous or teleoperated robotic systems capable of non-lethal force raises major international debates over safety regulations and robotic laws of engagement.
A company named Unitree introduced a humanoid machine called the Guardian.
The newly revealed automaton is intended to serve as a personal protector in real life.
Reported capabilities for the device include the ability to hoist automobiles.
The machine is also claimed to be capable of subduing hostile individuals.
The enterprise responsible for the creation is identified as a major producer of humanoid machines globally.
A claim was made that the organization is working on artificial intelligence to allow these machines to enhance their own capabilities (plan).
Reports noted that humanoid machines from the same source are seeking employment opportunities in South Korea.
